- 2026-06-29 13:17:15 +0800 - Watchdog: act immediately on a deep functional-probe wedge
  - Status: Pushed
  - Areas changed: `scripts/fleet-health-watchdog.mjs`
  - Summary: Fixes a real gap found while testing the deep probes against a live NYC TTS wedge: the cheap per-cycle probe (collector `/health`, TTS `/v1/models`) PASSES even when the deep functional probe (collector `/chat`, TTS synth) fails, so the shared consecutive-failure counter kept resetting between the 15-min deep cycles and a wedged-but-reachable backend would never reach the 3-strike remediation threshold. Deep functional failures are now flagged `severe` and remediate on a SINGLE occurrence (still gated by the 5-min cooldown), while cheap-probe failures keep the 3-strike tolerance for brief reload flaps. So a backend that's up-but-can't-actually-work is restarted on the next deep cycle, not never.
  - Verification: `node --check` clean. Verified live against an actually-wedged NYC TTS (synth returned 32B / 0B — the proxy-error blob): the deep probe correctly flagged it unhealthy. The wedge then self-cleared (NYC flapping), and the deep probe correctly read healthy again (synth → 38,776B real PCM). Every link is proven separately — wedge detection, healthy read, and the `kickstart universal-tts` remediation (proven by hand earlier this session when it restored 51 models) — even though the transient cleared before an automated remediation fired. Installed daemon reloaded with the change.
  - Intended commit message: `Watchdog: remediate immediately on a deep functional-probe wedge`
- 2026-06-29 13:12:04 +0800 - Add the deep TTS synth probe to the fleet health watchdog
  - Status: Pushed
  - Areas changed: `scripts/fleet-health-watchdog.mjs`
  - Summary: The watchdog's TTS check now also runs a deep probe every 15th cycle — it actually POSTs a tiny `/v1/audio/speech-stream` synth and requires real PCM back (≥2KB). This catches the last uncovered failure: the TTS frontend up (so `/v1/models` still returns the static catalog) but the model backend WEDGED, where no audio comes out. The cold-load false positive is handled by judging on the RESULT (bytes) under a generous 60s timeout, so a slow-but-real cold model load passes while a wedged backend (instant proxy-error blob, or a >60s hang) fails. Tunable via `FLEET_WATCHDOG_TTS_{DEEP_TIMEOUT_MS,MODEL,VOICE}` (defaults chatterbox-turbo/voice01, the fast proven path). Same 3-strike + 5-min-cooldown remediation as the rest.
  - Verification: `node --check` clean. Ran live with the deep probe forced: it synthesized on the NYC TTS and returned real PCM → `cycle 0: 3 healthy, 0 unhealthy of 3 (deep probe: collector chat + TTS synth)`. Installed LaunchAgent reloaded. This closes the frontend-up/backend-wedged gap noted in the prior two watchdog entries; the only remaining named caveat is external memory pressure (Splashtop ~16GB on NYC), which no restart can fix.
  - Intended commit message: `Add deep TTS synth probe to the fleet health watchdog`
- 2026-06-29 02:50:19 +0800 - Extend the fleet health watchdog to the Universal TTS server
  - Status: Pushed
  - Areas changed: `scripts/fleet-health-watchdog.mjs`
  - Summary: The watchdog now also watches each machine's Universal TTS server, not just the collector — so a TTS flap self-heals the same way (the voice-side instability from this session). It discovers TTS apps via `/api/fleet/apps` (port 8799 / `universal-tts`), probes `/v1/models` reachable+non-empty (which fails with a proxy EOF when the stack is down — the flapping case; `/v1/voices` was rejected as a probe because it 307-redirects through the linkd app-proxy), and on 3 consecutive failures restarts the `universal-tts` service on the owning machine via the linkd shell. Collector and TTS are keyed separately, so a TTS flap restarts ONLY the TTS daemon and a collector flap restarts ONLY the collector. The kickstart pattern is specific (`universal.?tts|mlx.?audio`) so it won't hit the unrelated mlx image sidecar.
  - Verification: `node --check` clean. Ran live against the real fleet: now 3 targets (NYC collector, Ubuntu VPS collector, NYC TTS) → `cycle 0: 3 healthy, 0 unhealthy of 3`; the installed LaunchAgent was reloaded and confirmed the same in its log. Mid-test it also correctly caught a real NYC collector flap (`chat HTTP 502 … EOF`, counted 1/3) and recovered — exactly the detection it's there for. A deep synth probe (to catch frontend-up/backend-down) is a deliberate follow-up, left out of v1 to avoid cold-model-load false positives.
  - Intended commit message: `Extend fleet health watchdog to the Universal TTS server`
- 2026-06-29 02:35:14 +0800 - Add a fleet health watchdog (auto-restart wedged collectors)
  - Status: Pushed
  - Areas changed: new `scripts/fleet-health-watchdog.mjs` daemon + `scripts/install-fleet-health-watchdog.sh` (LaunchAgent/systemd installer), `package.json` (`fleet-watchdog` / `fleet-watchdog:install` scripts)
  - Summary: A standalone daemon that, from the dashboard host, rediscovers the connected machines each cycle (via the local `/api/fleet/discover`, no pinned tailnet IPs; falls back to a cached list when the dashboard is closed) and probes each remote machine's agent collector — cheap `/health` every cycle (60s) plus a deep `/chat` dispatch every 15th cycle. After 3 consecutive failures it force-restarts that machine's collector by running a `launchctl kickstart` (macOS) / `systemctl restart` (Linux) over the **hive-native linkd shell** (`/_hivemind/shell/`), then cools down 5 min. This closes the gap launchd `KeepAlive` / systemd `Restart` cannot cover: the daemon being ALIVE but functionally broken (the `spawn EBADF` wedge seen this session) or a prolonged outage — `KeepAlive` only relaunches on process *exit*. Pure Node (no build step), env-tunable, logs to `~/.hivemindos/fleet-health-watchdog.log`. v1 watches the collector (the delegation-critical path); extending the probe + kickstart pattern to the Universal TTS service is a small follow-up.
  - Root cause it addresses (diagnosed live on the NYC box via the linkd shell): collector + TTS both have `KeepAlive=true` (so they DO relaunch on exit — `last exit code = 1, runs = 3`), but the collector also auto-reloads on source change (exits+relaunches → the brief "flapping" unreachability windows), and a wedged-but-alive state (`spawn EBADF`) is invisible to KeepAlive. Memory pressure is real but external (Splashtop ~16GB resident) — flagged, not touched.
  - Verification: `node --check` clean; `bash -n` clean on the installer; `package.json` re-parsed valid. Ran live against the real fleet (`FLEET_WATCHDOG_ONCE=1`): discovered 2 remote machines (NYC macOS + the Ubuntu VPS) with no pinned IPs, deep-probed both → `cycle 0: 2 healthy, 0 unhealthy of 2` (no false remediation). Installed the LaunchAgent on This Mac (`com.hivemindos.fleet-health-watchdog`, running, heartbeat logging). The remediation path reuses the exact `launchctl kickstart` that recovered NYC by hand earlier this session. NOT verified: a live remediation trigger (would require deliberately wedging a collector) — the kickstart command itself is proven; the failure-count→remediate logic is straightforward and gated by threshold + cooldown.
  - Intended commit message: `Add fleet health watchdog (auto-restart wedged collectors via linkd shell)`
- 2026-06-29 02:13:16 +0800 - Honor explicit machine targeting in Queen Bee routing
  - Status: Pushed
  - Areas changed: Queen Bee router (`src/lib/services/queen-bee/router.ts`), control plane (`src/lib/services/queen-bee/control-plane.ts`)
  - Summary: The Queen Bee router now honors an explicit machine target as a HARD pin — previously the `machineId` queue-task param (and any in-message "run on machine X") was silently dropped, so the router always picked the highest-scoring agent fleet-wide and a task meant for the NYC MacBook kept running on This Mac. `QueenBeeRouterOptions` gained `targetMachineKey`; when set, `rankQueenBeeDelegates` restricts candidates to that one machine's agents (matched by key, friendly name, machineId, dnsName, or dnsName first label via the new exported `machineMatchesTarget`), so the autonomous-pickup fallback chain rotates only among THAT machine's agents instead of routing elsewhere. - 2026-06-28 16:47:08 +0800 - Queen voice chat honors the Local TTS call setting
  - Status: Pushed
  - Areas changed: `src/app/api/queen-bee/voice/route.ts` (the `speak` front door + GET now exposes `localTtsSelected`), `src/lib/services/phone/local-tts.ts` (new buffered `synthesizeLocalTtsWav` + `pcm16ToWav` helper), `src/lib/services/queen-bee/voice-settings.ts` (new `readQueenBeeCallPreferences`), `src/features/queen-voice/QueenBeeVoiceOverlay.tsx` (route to the pipeline when local TTS is selected)
  - Summary: The in-app Queen Bee voice chat overlay now voices its spoken replies through the Local TTS server selected in the Queen's Calls settings, instead of always using OpenAI cloud TTS. Two root causes were fixed. (1) The `speak` action was hardcoded to OpenAI and ignored the agent's `calls` voice runtime; it now reads the Queen profile's persisted Calls prefs server-side and, when `voiceRuntime === "local-tts"` (or a `local-tts:` provider id is set), resolves the validated candidate via the existing `resolveLocalTtsCallConfig`, synthesizes on that server, and returns it. Because the overlay decodes a complete clip with `decodeAudioData` (it does not stream PCM frames), the new `synthesizeLocalTtsWav` requests PCM with `realtime_pacing: false`, buffers it, and wraps it in a 44-byte PCM16 WAV (`audio/wav`). (2) The decisive one: the overlay DEFAULTS to OpenAI Realtime (`realtimeMode` is true until a realtime session fails), and Realtime is speech-to-speech straight to OpenAI — it never calls `speak`, so local TTS could never apply. The overlay now fetches the Queen's selection on open (`GET /api/queen-bee/voice` → `localTtsSelected`) and, when local TTS is selected, runs the non-realtime STT→converse→`speak` pipeline instead of Realtime; both voice hooks are gated until that resolves so a local-TTS selection never briefly starts a Realtime session. The Queen is resolved exactly as the dashboard does for the chat FAB + Queen settings (`agents.find(beeRole === "queen")`, then name match) so the prefs read are the same single profile the user edits. Any miss falls through to OpenAI → browser speech synthesis.
  - Streaming playback (latency): added `POST {action:"speak-stream"}` + `streamLocalTtsPcm` (overlay params: `realtime_pacing:false`, no `lowpass_hz`, distinct from the mobile `streamLocalTtsSpeech`) which forwards the local TTS PCM frame stream as `audio/pcm` (+ `x-audio-sample-rate`/`x-audio-channels`). `use-queen-bee-voice.ts` gained `playStreamedLocalTts`, which schedules PCM16 chunks back-to-back on the VAD AudioContext (gapless, carries odd trailing bytes across chunks, ~150ms lead-in) so audio starts as frames arrive instead of after the whole clip; the overlay passes `streamLocalTts` (true only when local TTS is the resolved engine). Any miss → 409 `{fallback:true}` → client falls back to the buffered `speak` path → OpenAI → browser synth. Logs `stage:"speak-stream"` telemetry with first-byte `ttsMs`.
  - Telemetry: `~/.hivemindos/queen-voice-telemetry.jsonl` now records `stage:"speak"` and `stage:"speak-stream"` lines per spoken reply with the `engine` actually used (`local-tts` | `openai` | `none`), the resolved voice/model (and appName/appId/audioBytes/sampleRate), `ttsMs`, and a `localFallbackReason` when a selected local TTS server was tried but missed.
  - Model + Voice pickers (Calls panel): the local-TTS candidate now carries `availableModels` (full `/v1/models`, deduped — server lists `tts-1` twice) and `availableVoices` (full `/v1/voices`), and `AgentSettingsCallsPanel` renders "Model (this agent)" and "Voice (this agent)" `<select>`s for the chosen candidate that write `voiceModelId`/`voiceId` through the dashboard's own save path. `validateCandidate` was only exposing the selected provider's 2 chatterbox model ids.
  - Cloned-voice leak (diagnosed, NOT our bug): `voice01` is a clone that replays its reference clip ("…the soldier we needed you to be") before the reply. Reproduced server-side: `voice01` → 4.0s of audio for input "Hi." across EVERY model, while real voices that aren't clones render short — so it's the voice/clone on the universal-tts server, not our request (we send only the reply text). The voice picker lets the user switch to `voice01-xvector` (embedding-based, expected clean) or another voice; unconfirmed because the TTS server went unreachable mid-test (`hivemind-linkd proxy error: EOF`, capabilities `http=000`) — the same NYC-box flakiness behind the recurring 502 → OpenAI `nova` fallbacks. This is the durable fix for model selection: a direct edit to the stored profile gets clobbered by the running app re-persisting its in-memory roster (observed live — a hand-set `qwen3-tts-1.7b-custom` reverted to `chatterbox-turbo` between turns), so the model MUST be set in-app to stick. NOTE on latency: warm, every model streams first audio in ~0.6–1.1s (measured qwen 0.69s, kokoro 0.66s, chatterbox 0.64s, vibevoice-realtime 1.15s); the "extremely slow" reports were cold model loads (~5–30s on first call after the server idles/swaps, which can trip the 30s buffered timeout → OpenAI `nova` fallback) plus the reverted-to-chatterbox model — not the streaming path.
  - Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on all touched files (repo-wide count holds at the pre-existing baseline; only generated `.next-tauri-build/types` validators for unrelated routes fluctuate). `npx eslint` clean. WAV header unit-checked. **Verified live end-to-end** (dev app port 5121, real `universal-tts` server on the NYC Mac over tailnet, voice01): `GET`→`localTtsSelected:true`; `POST {action:"speak"}`→`audio/wav`; `POST {action:"speak-stream"}`→`audio/pcm` + sample-rate headers + raw PCM16; buffered `speak` regression-checked (`audio/wav`); telemetry shows `engine:"local-tts"` for both `speak` and `speak-stream`. LATENCY (qwen3-tts-1.7b-custom over cross-planet tailnet): warm full-clip `ttsMs` ~8–9s; stream first-byte 0.8s (long input, early chunks) to ~5s (short input, single segment); a cold model load is ~30s and trips the buffered 30s timeout → OpenAI fallback (so the first reply after idle may be OpenAI `nova`). The server/model/network is the floor, not our code. NOT confirmed by ear in the live overlay (gapless client scheduling + the "speaks a turn late" symptom can only be confirmed by the user after reloading the app).

- 2026-06-19 16:10:00 +0700 - Agent flows: graph/crew orchestration layer for the Queen Bee
  - Status: Pushed
  - Areas changed: New flow layer (`src/lib/types/agent-flow.ts`, `src/lib/services/queen-bee/flow-engine.ts`, `flow-templates.ts`, `flow-runner.ts`, `src/app/api/queen-bee/flow/route.ts`); company process (`src/lib/types/company.ts`, `src/lib/services/companies-orchestration.ts`); test (`scripts/test-agent-flow.mjs`, `package.json`)
  - Summary: Adds the missing composition layer that turns HivemindOS's existing crew (Company) + single-node loop (KanbanLoopSpec) into LangGraph/CrewAI-style flows. A FlowSpec is nodes (worker-class steps or human-approval checkpoints) wired by conditional edges (success/failure/score thresholds), with a shared state object threaded through each step. A pure engine evaluates edges, loops back bounded by a step cap + per-node retry, pauses for human-in-the-loop approval, and terminates on DONE/FAIL — modelling research → draft → (quality < bar ? back to research : publish) → approve. A runner submits each node's task via the Queen Bee (reusing routing/receipts) and advances when a node completes. Companies gain a `process` field: "hierarchical" (default, unchanged parallel fan-out), "sequential" (CrewAI-style ordered chain, each step consuming the prior output), or "graph" (run a saved FlowSpec). Built-in templates ship and user flows persist to the vault under Operations/Flows. New API: GET/POST `/api/queen-bee/flow` (list/get templates + runs, save-template, start, advance, resolve-approval).
  - Verification: `npm run test:agent-flow` passes — exercises the branch+bounded-loop+HITL flow (research runs twice on a sub-bar score, then publishes and waits for approval), the step-cap killing an infinite loop, approval-rejection routing to FAIL, the sequential builder + {{state}}/{{last}} prompt rendering, and the runner driving a full run via injected mock dispatch with vault persistence. `tsc --noEmit` adds no new errors (total unchanged at the pre-existing baseline). Router/MCP/packaged-agents gates still pass. The default `hierarchical` company path is untouched (guarded behind the new `process` check). NOT done / follow-up: automatic worker-side advancement (today the executor advances via the POST advance API; the autonomous worker was left untouched to avoid destabilizing the live loop, since task source is carried in the task body not a field), and a flow-builder UI.

  - Summary: Fixes the Windows-only "HivemindOS couldn't start its local server" error that hit every Windows install since the first embedded release (v0.2.10). The Tauri runtime hands Node the embedded server path in Windows extended-length (verbatim) form (`\\?\C:\...\server.js`); Node realpath-resolves the main module at startup and crashes on that form with `EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, lstat 'C:'`, so the dashboard backend never booted and every launch (and "rerun setup") landed on the error page. The fix launches Node with `--preserve-symlinks-main`, which skips the realpath of the entry script while keeping the long-path-safe prefix. macOS/Linux are unaffected.

NOTE: a fully-broken Windows install can't auto-update (the updater runs in the dashboard, which never loaded), so affected users must download the fixed build once.
  - Intended commit message: `Fix Windows embedded server boot: --preserve-symlinks-main (EISDIR on \\?\ path)`

## 2026-06-13 10:52:28 +0700 - Fix Stuck Dashboard Loading Screen And Add Issue Reporting

- Status: Pushed
- Areas changed: dashboard hydration loader (`src/lib/services/dashboard-state-client.ts`, `src/features/dashboard/DashboardApp.tsx`), new client issue reporter (`src/lib/utils/issue-reporter.ts`), new Cloudflare Worker (`workers/issues/`)
- Summary: Fixes the bug where a fresh install could sit forever on a loading screen ("Scanning fleet discovery" on the desktop, "Opening Agent Chat" on mobile). Both screens gate on dashboard hydration, which only completed after the local-state snapshot loaded — and that loader retried `/api/dashboard/state` indefinitely with no give-up, so any persistent backend failure left the app on an endless spinner. The retry is preserved (it protects stored chat history from an empty-boot overwrite), but after ~10s of failure the app now shows a recoverable "Still connecting to HivemindOS…" screen with a Reload button that clears itself the moment the service answers. Broken boots are also reported (anonymized: failure kind, HTTP status, app version, coarse UA, random per-install id — never user content, paths, secrets, or IPs) to a new `hivemindos-issues` Cloudflare Worker + D1, so a stuck install is visible centrally without asking the user to open devtools.
- Verification: `tsc`/`eslint` clean on all changed files; `pnpm test:dashboard-state-snapshot` green (no-data-loss semantics preserved); issues Worker deployed and round-trip verified live (POST accepted, token-gated read works, unauthorized → 401). The loading screen itself is Tauri-only and needs a desktop build for a live look.
- Intended commit message: `Fix dashboard loading-screen hang; add anonymized issue reporting`

## 2026-06-12 19:07:50 +0700 - Fix Windows Production Build EPERM By Hiding homedir() From Build Tracing

- Status: Pushed
- Areas changed: new opaque home-dir helper (`src/lib/home-dir.ts`), homedir import swap across 71 server/source files (`src/**`), setup E2E workflow diagnostics (`.github/workflows/setup-e2e-matrix.yml`), tracing diagnostics scripts (`scripts/trace-profile-scandir.cjs`, `scripts/instrument-compiled-glob.cjs`)
- Summary: `next build --webpack` failed on every Windows machine with `EPERM: operation not permitted, scandir C:\Users\<user>\...` (Cookies/Application Data junctions). Root cause, proven with module-level instrumentation of Next's bundled glob and `@vercel/nft`: nft's static evaluator models the real `os` module, so every traced `join(homedir(), <dynamic>)` in server code emitted the whole user profile as an asset-directory glob (`C:\Users\<user>/**/*`), which EPERMs on protected Windows junctions and also silently walked the entire home directory during macOS/Linux builds. Fix: `homedir()` is now re-exported through `src/lib/home-dir.ts` behind an indirection nft cannot statically evaluate, and all `src/` imports of `homedir` from `os` were swapped to the helper (call sites unchanged).
- Verification: direct nft probes reproduce the emission with a plain `os` homedir import and show zero emissions through the helper; full sandboxed macOS production build with instrumented nft confirms zero home-rooted asset emissions and a successful build; windows-latest CI confirms zero profile-rooted asset emissions with the helper in place (the unfixed commit reproduced them as a negative control). The remaining Windows failure was a plain V8 heap OOM (exit 134): `setup.ps1` now builds with `--max-old-space-size=8192`, and the CI diagnose job is replaced by a strict `next build` job on windows-latest, which passed green (run 27419483805) alongside the full setup matrix on ubuntu, macOS, and Windows.
- Intended commit message: `Hide homedir from build tracing to fix Windows next build EPERM`

## 2026-06-12 14:33:17 +07 +0700 - Make Adaptive Agents Reliable: Learned Model Routing, Quality Gates, And Fleet Gossip

- Status: Pushed
- Areas changed: agent-runtime route (`src/app/api/chat/agent-runtime/route.ts`), adaptive model resolver (`src/lib/services/chat/adaptive-openrouter-models.ts`), new reliability/quality module (`src/lib/services/chat/adaptive-model-reliability.ts`), telemetry collector (`scripts/agent-telemetry-collector.mjs`), docs (`docs/features/runtimes-and-chat.md`, `docs/features/index.md`)
- Summary: Adaptive Hermes agents (model `adaptive`, provider `openrouter`) were unusable for long tasks and re-rolled the free-model lottery every message. Root cause of the "stuck agent" report: the adaptive path enforced a hard 45-second wall clock per model attempt and disabled Hermes session resume, so any task longer than 45s (e.g. multi-leg flight research) was killed and restarted from scratch up to 6 times, then failed — visible as a new "Attached Hermes session" every ~45s. Fixes, in order: (1) the 45s timer now only covers time-to-first-stream-byte; once flowing, the idle window is 15 minutes and the route emits a bare SSE keepalive comment every 25s so the browser's 130s stall timer survives silent tool work, and failed attempts resume the prior Hermes CLI session (`--resume`) with the next candidate model instead of restarting. (2) New learned reliability store at `~/.hivemindos/openrouter-model-reliability.json` (5s TTL re-read, atomic-write safe): routing sticks to the most recent model that completed a quality-passing request; failures classify from error text/status — capacity (429/quota/overloaded) cools a model 5min doubling per consecutive hit capped at 6h, unsupported 24h, other failures 15min; cooled models drop to the back of the candidate list rather than out of it; one success fully resets a model. (3) Evo-inspired quality gates: every completed response is graded (`assessAdaptiveResponseQuality`) — dead-end refusals, unrequested prompt echoes, and repetition loops record a `low-quality` outcome ("completed but useless" still demotes); a second consecutive low-quality response benches the model 10min doubling per repeat; under 50% pass ratio across 3+ graded responses ranks below never-tried models; responses still reach the user, grading only changes future routing. (4) Fleet gossip: collectors serve `GET /reliability/openrouter` and merge peer stores newest-wins per model id every 10 minutes (`AGENT_TELEMETRY_RELIABILITY_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS`, `0` disables; `POST /reliability/sync` manual trigger), discovering peers from `tailscale status --json` deduplicated by machineId — the fleet shares one OpenRouter key, so one machine's rate limit now benches that model fleet-wide within a cycle; payloads are model ids and counters only, no secrets or persisted tailnet IPs. Gossip activates per machine as its collector restarts with the new script.
- Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean for touched files (two pre-existing unrelated errors remain in `next.config.ts` and the Remotion video); eslint clean on touched files; `node --check scripts/agent-telemetry-collector.mjs`; isolated unit suites under a temp HOME pass (19 gate/ordering/cooldown assertions plus TTL re-read and escalation-cap checks). Live E2E against the running dev server with a real adaptive agent: simple prompts complete in ~7-20s; the same model leads consecutive messages; an injected capacity cooldown rerouted the next message to a different free model without touching the cooled one; a 50-second silent shell task survived in a single Hermes session with keepalives observed at 25s intervals and delivered its answer at 63s (old behavior: killed at 45s); a quality pass was recorded through the real route. Collector gossip E2E with two isolated instances (distinct temp HOMEs/machine ids, stubbed tailnet): peer store served, sync adopted 2 fresher records including a 429 cooldown, second sync adopted 0 (idempotent); test instances stopped and temp state removed. Production collectors still run the pre-change script until their next restart.
- Intended commit message: `Make adaptive agents reliable with learned routing, quality gates, and fleet gossip`
- Follow-up (same session): the Adaptive provider (`provider: adaptive`, routing across OpenRouter plus Models.dev OpenAI-compatible providers) now has full parity. Reliability store keys namespace non-OpenRouter providers as `provider::model-id` (OpenRouter stays bare-id, so existing stores and collector gossip are unchanged); `resolveAdaptiveRoutePlan` reorders candidates from every provider by observed reliability ahead of keyword scores (cooling models sink, quality-demoted rank below never-tried, most recent quality-passing winner leads); the direct-API attempt loop records capacity/unsupported/failure outcomes per attempt and grades the completed response through the same quality gate before recording success; and a Hermes-selected plan re-shapes to the adaptive-OpenRouter profile so it gets the full optimized loop (per-message failover, session resume, keepalives, quality gates) instead of pinning one model with no failover. Note: a parallel session had rebuilt the agent-runtime route from HEAD (reasoning-content/`<think>` handling), dropping the earlier adaptive wiring; all of it was re-applied on top alongside the parity work. Verification: tsc/eslint clean on touched files (remaining tsc errors come from other in-flight uncommitted work in `agent-profile-store.ts`/`runtime-integrations.ts`); 12 new isolated unit assertions for key namespacing, reliability states, and quality demotion pass; live E2E: real adaptive-agent regression (success + quality recording confirmed in the store), a synthetic `provider: adaptive` hivemind-os profile completed via the direct-API path and recorded success through the quality gate, and a synthetic Hermes-runtime adaptive-provider profile completed via the re-shaped optimized loop — all three runs selected the same store-proven winner, confirming reliability stickiness now crosses both paths. Docs updated in `docs/features/runtimes-and-chat.md`.

## 2026-06-12 14:15:00 WITA +0800 - Make Shared Env Sync Self-Healing With Retry Queue And Periodic Pull-Reconcile

- Status: Pushed
- Areas changed: shared env CLI (`scripts/hive-env-add`), telemetry collector (`scripts/agent-telemetry-collector.mjs`), shared env docs (`docs/whole-brain/shared-env.md`), new focused test (`scripts/test-env-sync-queue.mjs`)
- Summary: Shared env replication between machines was push-once and fire-and-forget: if a peer's collector was down or unreachable at the moment of `hive-env-add`, the key silently never arrived, and peers that failed the health probe were silently dropped from sync accounting entirely. Env sync is now self-healing. (1) Retry queue: updates (including removals) that do not reach every peer are queued in `~/.hivemindos/env-sync-pending.json` (key names, scope/runtime, and per-machine delivery receipts only — never secret values); every later sync-enabled run drains the queue, `hive-env-add --retry-pending` drains it manually, and entries expire after 14 days. (2) Periodic pull-reconcile: each collector runs `hive-env-add --sync-maintenance` every 10 minutes (configurable via `AGENT_TELEMETRY_ENV_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS`, off via `AGENT_TELEMETRY_ENV_SYNC_DISABLED=1`), which retries the queue then merges shared keys from every ready peer collector newest-wins by per-key `updatedAt` metadata; locally removed keys keep a meta timestamp tombstone so peers cannot resurrect them, and a local key with unknown age is never overwritten blind. New `hive-env-add --pull-reconcile [--dry-run]`, collector `POST /env/sync-maintenance` trigger, and maintenance status in collector `/health` under `envSync.maintenance`. Peer discovery improvements: peers without a ready collector are now reported (and queued for) instead of silently skipped, the health probe timeout rose from 2s to 4s for slow links, the two tailnet nodes every HivemindOS machine has (system tailscaled + embedded link node) are deduplicated by machine id, the local machine's own link node is excluded, phones are excluded from retry accounting, and an explicit `HIVE_ENV_COLLECTOR_PORTS` list is now authoritative (defaults are not appended). Root cause of the triggering incident: `~/.local/.env.local` pinned `HIVE_ENV_TAILNET_TARGETS` to a stale IP for the NYC MacBook plus the down Hetzner VPS, blackholing every push from this machine; the pinned line is commented out in favor of auto-discovery, and the missing `SWARM_SOVEREIGN_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` was delivered to the NYC MacBook through the new retry queue.
- Verification: `python3 -m py_compile scripts/hive-env-add`; `node --check scripts/agent-telemetry-collector.mjs`; new `node scripts/test-env-sync-queue.mjs` passes (queueing on failed push, drain to a stub peer collector, immediate-delivery non-queueing, queued removal propagation, pull-reconcile remote-only/newer/older/tombstone matrix with timestamp adoption, `--sync-maintenance` JSON); existing `node scripts/test-hive-env-remove.mjs` and `node scripts/test-aeon-env-auto-sync.mjs` still pass. Live E2E on the real tailnet: simulated failed push queued `HIVE_E2E_RETRY_QUEUE_PROBE`, `--retry-pending` delivered it to the NYC MacBook (value verified via its collector `GET /env`), queued removal also propagated; `--pull-reconcile` imported `LM_STUDIO_BASE_URL`/`LM_STUDIO_MODEL` from the NYC machine with origin timestamps adopted; local collector restarted via launchd and `POST /env/sync-maintenance` plus `/health` `envSync.maintenance` verified live; `SWARM_SOVEREIGN_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` confirmed present on the NYC machine. `node scripts/test-vault-structure-contract.mjs` fails on a pre-existing unrelated assertion about `src/lib/types/agent-runtime.ts` (`kanbanFolder`), unchanged by this work.
- Intended commit message: `Make shared env sync self-healing with retry queue and pull-reconcile`
- Follow-up (same session): the stale pin was written by the fleet E2E itself — `configureEnvSyncTargets()` in `scripts/e2e-real-fleet.mjs` POSTs raw-IP `HIVE_ENV_TAILNET_TARGETS` (scope `all`, landing in `~/.local/.env.local` on installed machines) and never cleaned up, permanently reconfiguring production sync targets fleet-wide. The env suite now clears the pin on every tested machine in a `finally` (recorded under `summary.cleanup` as `env-sync-targets`). `hive-env-add` warnings now append a `[targets pinned via HIVE_ENV_TAILNET_TARGETS…]` hint whenever a pin is the source of sync targets. The setup-installed "Shared Hive Env" instruction block (`scripts/seed-shared-skills.sh`) and the vault skill `Skills/shared-hive-env/SKILL.md` now document the self-healing sync behavior and the never-pin rule. Verification: `node --check scripts/e2e-real-fleet.mjs`; `bash -n scripts/seed-shared-skills.sh`; `python3 -m py_compile scripts/hive-env-add`; `node scripts/test-env-sync-queue.mjs` and `node scripts/test-hive-env-remove.mjs` re-pass; updated CLI reinstalled to `~/.local/bin`.

## 2026-06-12 12:35:19 +07 +0700 - Fix Native Setup Launch And Add Cross-Platform Setup E2E

- Status: Pushed
- Areas changed: native setup invoke wrapper (`src/lib/native/setup.ts`), Tauri setup command (`src-tauri/src/setup.rs`), Windows setup scripts (`setup.ps1`, `uninstall.ps1`), Next config (`next.config.ts`), setup E2E workflow (`.github/workflows/setup-e2e-matrix.yml`)
- Summary: The desktop first-run setup ("just this computer" and the other install modes) failed immediately with `command native_setup_run missing required key request` because the frontend passed the setup options flat instead of nested under the Tauri command's `request` parameter. The invoke payload is now wrapped correctly, the Rust request struct rejects unknown fields so future frontend/Rust payload drift fails loudly, the setup command builder is extracted into a testable function with unit tests covering the exact frontend payload, and a new CI workflow exercises the generated setup command plus full non-interactive setup on macOS, Linux, and Windows runners. The Windows E2E run caught a second bug: `setup.ps1` crashed at the shared-skills instruction-block step on every machine because PowerShell unrolled the list returned by `Remove-HivemindManagedBlock` (empty list became `$null`, populated list a fixed-size array), breaking `.Add()`; the function now returns the list intact via the comma operator. The re-run then caught a third Windows bug: `setup.ps1`'s Claude hook installer (and three `uninstall.ps1` helpers) assigned to `$home`, which is a read-only automatic variable in PowerShell 7, crashing every Windows setup; the variables are renamed to `$homeDir`. A fourth Windows bug followed: assigning `@($filteredGroups)` (a wrapped `List[object]`) into the hooks hashtable threw `Argument types do not match` in the Claude hook installer in `setup.ps1` and its `uninstall.ps1` mirror; both now assign `$filteredGroups.ToArray()`. The Windows E2E also exposed that `setup.ps1` ignored pnpm exit codes: a failed production build printed `✓ Dashboard built` and stamped the build cache so re-runs would skip the broken build, and the lingering exit code made an otherwise successful setup report failure. Dependency install failures are now fatal, build failures warn without stamping the cache (the dev server compiles on demand), and the script exits 0 explicitly on success. A known open issue remains: `next build --webpack` fails on Windows with `EPERM: scandir C:\Users\<user>\Cookies` (something in the Next 16 webpack build walks the user profile); the dev-server path is unaffected. Two cleanups followed: the unsupported `eslint` key is removed from `next.config.ts` (Next 16 dropped built-in ESLint integration, so the key only produced an invalid-config warning on every boot), and the Windows E2E job verifies the dashboard inside the setup step because Windows runners kill step-spawned child processes between steps — the round-6 diagnostics proved the dev server boots cleanly on Windows and was only being reaped by the runner. The Windows native setup path is now implemented end to end: `native_setup_run` previously wrote a bash `.command` file invoking `./setup.sh` even on Windows, which could never run; a `SetupPlatform` matrix in `src-tauri/src/setup.rs` now generates a `.cmd` launcher that clones/uses the repo and runs `setup.ps1` via pwsh (falling back to Windows PowerShell), maps the request flags (`-SkipDashboard`, `-SkipBuild`, `-SkipDeps`, `-Force`), uses `where` instead of `sh -lc` for command detection, and reports `setup.ps1`/winget install commands in `native_setup_status`. Both PowerShell scripts also gained a 5.1 guard that re-execs into pwsh (installing it via winget when missing) since fresh Windows lacks PowerShell 7 and the scripts use `-AsHashtable`. The 5.1 CI entry test then caught that both scripts were saved as UTF-8 without a BOM: Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads BOM-less files as ANSI, so the ✓/✗ characters corrupted parsing before the re-exec guard could run; both scripts now carry a UTF-8 BOM.
- Verification: `cargo test --lib setup::` passes (5 tests) in `src-tauri`; sandboxed local macOS E2E (isolated HOME, port 5841) ran the exact generated native command and a full non-interactive setup with the dashboard answering HTTP 200; `test/setup-e2e-matrix` branch CI runs `setup.sh` E2E green on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest, and `setup.ps1` on windows-latest (failed before the PowerShell fix, re-run after).
- Intended commit message: `Fix native setup invoke payload and add setup E2E matrix`

- Areas changed: Fleet agent delete tombstones (`src/features/fleet/fleet-identity.ts`, `src/features/dashboard/hooks/use-wallet-files-controller.tsx`), dashboard-state boot snapshot loader (`src/lib/services/dashboard-state-client.ts`), tests (`scripts/test-fleet-agent-suppression.mjs`, new `scripts/test-dashboard-state-snapshot.mjs`, `package.json`)
- Summary: Deleting a duplicate agent entry no longer hides the agent you kept. Duplicate roster entries that point at the same runtime workspace share a workspace tombstone, so removing the stale copy used to make both vanish from the Fleet graph (live incident: BankrAgent disappeared after its stale duplicate was deleted). Deletes now record only tombstone keys that no surviving saved profile resolves to, via the new `suppressionKeysForRemovedAgent` helper. Separately, the dashboard boot snapshot loader no longer treats a transient state-API outage (restarting dev server, proxy 503) as an empty snapshot: it retries with backoff until the server answers instead of booting empty and letting the next persist overwrite stored values — the mechanism that had been wiping saved chat history. Definitive non-5xx answers (such as auth denied) still resolve immediately and are never cached. Live state was also repaired: the BankrAgent workspace tombstone was removed, the stale duplicate profile was dropped from the roster, and today's BankrAgent chat thread was restored from its runtime session file.
- Verification: `pnpm test:fleet-agent-suppression` passed including new duplicate-delete regression cases; new `pnpm test:dashboard-state-snapshot` passed (retry-through-outage, 503-as-outage, definitive-answer paths); focused `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` returned no diagnostics for touched files; real-data check ran the transpiled `filterSuppressedAgents` against the repaired live `dashboard-state.json` and confirmed `hermes-bankragent-f15dbb` is visible in both saved-profile and discovered-machine sources. In-app Fleet graph confirmation pending a dashboard reload.
- Intended commit message: `Keep surviving duplicate agents visible and retry empty boot snapshots`

A new Playwright script (`scripts/e2e-queen-voice-overlay.mjs`) verifies the overlay end-to-end in a browser: unlock, toggle event, glow layers, and listening state.
- Verification: `node scripts/e2e-queen-voice-overlay.mjs` passed against the dev server (overlay mounted, 4 glow layers, status `Listening...`); breadcrumb log proved the tray click previously emitted two toggle events 19ms apart; `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/hivemindos-cargo-check cargo check` passed with zero warnings after the tao restore; `pnpm exec eslint` passed on touched TS files. ## 2026-06-09 18:35:44 WITA - Replace Local TTS Playback With AudioWorklet Stream Player

- Status: Pushed
- Areas changed: Local TTS call playback, shared browser PCM stream player, temporary VAD/STT harness diagnostics and continuous listening
- Summary: Local TTS calls now play streamed PCM through a shared AudioWorklet-backed player instead of scheduling each received PCM slice as a separate `AudioBufferSourceNode`. The new player keeps one continuous audio render thread, uses the browser's native output sample rate, waits for a 520ms startup jitter buffer, feeds PCM16 chunks into the worklet, resamples only when the incoming TTS rate differs from the output device, reports underruns, and never drops speech when the stream gets ahead. The production local-TTS call path no longer prepares or plays the cached "Got it." acknowledgement at speech end, so users hear only the actual orchestrated agent reply. The temporary realtime harness now imports the exact shared player module used by the app, includes a `Player Smoke` diagnostic backed by a deterministic paced PCM stream, and behaves like a continuous call: one click starts the mic/STT loop, each agent reply automatically returns to listening, and the same button can stop/send while listening or end the loop during a response.

Five-run direct Hivemind Link proxy benchmarks measured `chatterbox-turbo` / `voice01` at median first byte about `517ms` and first audible about `575ms` for `Yes.`, median first byte about `520ms` and first audible about `781ms` for a paralinguistic prompt, and median first byte about `505ms` and first audible about `1096ms` for a longer prompt while completion streamed over about `14330ms`; the `ResembleAI/chatterbox-turbo` alias measured median first byte about `485ms` and first audible about `491ms` for `Yes.`, about `467ms` / `593ms` for the paralinguistic prompt, and about `500ms` / `643ms` for the longer prompt. The already-running built app routes still added stale discovery/proxy overhead before rebuild, with `/api/fleet/apps/request` first audio about `17063ms` and `/api/phone` `local-tts-speech-stream` first audio about `14389ms` for the same `Yes.` request, so the source resolver/proxy fixes need the pending rebuild before the app route reflects the sub-second TTS path. Live diagnostics showed Universal's WAV 24 kHz and WAV 40 ms outputs are clean while the normal browser realtime player could still stutter, so the production source now requests `stream_frame_ms: 40`, `realtime_pacing: true`, `smooth_join_ms: 8`, and `lowpass_hz: 7000`; GitHub research identified AudioWorklet/ring-buffer players such as `wavtools`, `audio-worklet-stream`, and `pcm-ringbuf-player` as better long-term playback substrates than hand-scheduling `AudioBufferSource` chunks. `pnpm exec eslint src/lib/services/phone/local-tts.ts src/app/api/fleet/apps/request/route.ts src/features/dashboard/views/chat/AgentCallsSettingsPanel.tsx --max-warnings=999` passed; `node --check scripts/local-tts-vad-stt-harness.mjs` passed; focused `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit --pretty false 2>&1 | rg "src/(lib/services/phone/local-tts|app/api/fleet/apps/request/route|features/dashboard/views/chat/AgentCallsSettingsPanel)|scripts/local-tts-vad-stt-harness"` returned no touched-file diagnostics; `git diff --check -- src/lib/services/phone/local-tts.ts src/app/api/fleet/apps/request/route.ts scripts/local-tts-vad-stt-harness.mjs CHANGELOG.md` passed.

- Areas changed: Local TTS call setup, Local TTS streaming cache, phone VAD/STT, OpenAI Realtime STT client secrets, Whisper-compatible STT fallback config, phone voice-turn streaming, runtime voice latency mode, server-side Local TTS orchestration, orchestrator cancellation, exact agent call E2E harness, temporary VAD/STT harness
- Summary: Local TTS calls now skip redundant fleet validation when a selected TTS app/model/voice is already configured, and reuse the selected connected-app proxy for speech streaming instead of rediscovering fleet apps before every utterance. Local TTS turns now use HivemindOS as the realtime orchestrator: the client streams microphone PCM from Web Audio VAD into an OpenAI Realtime transcription session using a short-lived server-minted client secret, sends the final transcript directly to the phone API, the phone API streams the configured agent runtime, chunks speakable text earlier on the server, calls Universal TTS as a voice renderer, and returns one continuous PCM stream to the client. The older multipart Whisper-compatible STT path remains available as a fallback API path. Voice turns mark runtime requests with a low-latency voice mode so they skip slower task and shared-brain retrieval context while normal dashboard chat keeps the full context path. Client cancellation and barge-in now abort in-flight runtime/TTS fetches and stop scheduled playback as soon as the user starts speaking. Local TTS call setup preconnects Realtime STT, opportunistically prewarms Universal TTS, prebuffers a tiny cached `Got it.` PCM acknowledgement before listening, and logs first-byte plus first-audible timings for browser call measurements. The cached acknowledgement plays immediately at VAD speech-end so first audible response is not blocked by STT, LLM first token, or VibeVoice first-byte latency; generated agent speech still streams afterward when the runtime and TTS server produce it. The exact E2E call harness now preloads AdaptiveAgent and the validated Universal TTS candidate before the user clicks Start Local TTS call, so the modal exercises the real app call code without putting discovery latency in the click path. Voice-mode runtime parsing now treats runtime error frames as errors instead of speakable text, uses a short spoken-response instruction, filters reasoning/prompt preambles before sending text to TTS, and skips free OpenRouter Adaptive attempts for voice when a configured fallback model is available. AdaptiveAgent's OpenRouter fallback profile was changed from a slow DeepSeek fallback to `openai/gpt-4.1-mini` after live voice-path smokes showed current OpenRouter free models were exhausted and `openai/gpt-4.1-mini` returned text quickly.

- Summary: Add vault-native `remember`, `recall`, `answer`, and `rebuild-index` primitives for typed HivemindOS agent memories. Memories are stored as markdown under `Memory/Distillations/Agent Memory/`, indexed in the private materialized search log at `Operations/Brain Services/Agent Memory Index.jsonl`, and exposed through `/api/brain/memory` with type, tag, project, recency, confidence-aware recall, writer provenance fields for agent/runtime/machine/Tailnet identity, one-shot markdown-to-index rebuilds, and optional GitLawb memory receipts in `Operations/Brain Services/Agent Memory Proofs.jsonl` that store hashes/provenance without memory bodies. Agent runtime prompts, project instructions, the live shared-vault `AGENTS.md`, setup-generated vault contracts, macOS/Linux shared-skill seeding, Windows setup, and managed runtime hint blocks now tell agents to recall before relying on prior context, write durable shared memories through the API with machine/Tailnet provenance, use `proof: "auto"` by default, and avoid raw Tailnet IPs or secrets. `/api/chat/agent-runtime` now recalls matching shared-brain memories before dispatch and injects them into app-routed Hermes/OpenAI-compatible/OpenClaw contexts so runtimes do not need to independently decide to call memory. README and whole-brain docs include the measured local-first memory benchmarks and the private, network-free memory positioning.
- Summary addendum: Default `/api/brain/memory` recall/answer is now tiered instead of only reading the Agent Memory folder or always scanning the full vault: it checks typed Agent Memory first, returns the distilled layer when the top hit is strong, and otherwise augments with full-vault markdown. Callers can pass `scope: "agent-memory"` for strict typed/proven memory recall or `scope: "full-vault"` to force broad vault recall. Full-vault recall includes `Operations/Secure/` reference/status notes so agents can see credential names and set/missing status while plaintext secret values remain forbidden in notes, memory bodies, proofs, and responses. Full-vault records are cached briefly in-process after the cold local scan, and repeated scoring reuses normalized per-note search text.
- Summary addendum: Add the installed `hive-brain` command for raw/non-managed agents. `hive-brain answer "<query>"` and `hive-brain recall "<query>"` try the running `/api/brain/memory` route first and fall back to local vault/index search, so agents no longer need to know the dashboard port or be app-routed to check shared memory. `hive-brain remember` writes through the API with optional agent/runtime/machine/Tailnet provenance. Setup now installs `hive-brain`, uninstall removes it one-for-one, and the managed instruction blocks for Codex, Claude, Hermes, Gemini, OpenClaw, Aeon, plus the live vault and project Claude bridge, tell agents to run it before relying on prior context.
- Summary addendum: Add `hive-brain-hook` for runtime-native prompt injection. Setup now installs it next to `hive-brain` and registers it in `~/.claude/settings.json` as a Claude Code `UserPromptSubmit` hook, so raw Claude prompts receive shared-brain recall context before the model answers instead of merely being told to call a tool. Uninstall removes the hook entry one-for-one while preserving unrelated Claude settings. Runtime hint blocks also mention the hook while keeping the CLI/API path as the portable bridge for Hermes, Codex, Gemini, OpenClaw, Aeon, and other non-managed agents.
- Summary addendum: Refresh the GitHub Pages whole-brain architecture docs for the final memory shape: managed app injection, raw `hive-brain` CLI recall, Claude `hive-brain-hook` prompt injection, typed Agent Memory storage, private JSONL index, full-vault fallback for normal vault notes outside Agent Memory, `Operations/Secure` reference/status recall, and hash-only GitLawb memory proofs. The architecture sync page now names shared-memory access paths and hook/uninstall mirrors as required update surfaces, and the vault foundation seeder now teaches fresh vaults about the Claude hook.

## 2026-05-22 14:05 WITA - Move Agent Wallets Into Shared Brain

- Status: Pushed
- Areas changed: New `src/lib/services/obsidian/wallet-ledger.ts`, new `src/app/api/obsidian/wallets/route.ts`, hydrate + write-through effects in `src/app/page.tsx`, `machineName` surfaced on `AgentWalletCard`, changelog
- Summary: Move agent wallet state from device-local `localStorage` to the shared brain so balances follow the agent across machines. Each agent now has a human-readable record at `{vault}/Projects/HivemindOS/Wallets/{agentId}.md` with YAML frontmatter holding the full `AgentWalletConfig` plus metadata (`agentName`, `runtime`, `machineName`, `dashboardMachine`, `updatedAt`) and a brief markdown body summarising the current balance / status / network / runtime / last-write. New `GET /api/obsidian/wallets` lists the ledger and `POST /api/obsidian/wallets` upserts a single record. Dashboard hydrates from the vault on load when `sharedVault.enabled` (vault wins where `updatedAt` is newer than the local copy) and write-throughs each updated wallet with an 800ms debounce so slider drags and rapid edits coalesce. LocalStorage stays as an offline cache so the wallet view still works without the vault. The wallet card now shows the agent's home `machineName` in the subtitle row so cross-device balances are easy to attribute.
- Verification: `npm run typecheck` (no new errors; pre-existing apple-notes route warnings unchanged). Pattern matches the existing shared-brain integrations (`brain-graph.ts`, `brain-skills.ts`) — same `Projects/HivemindOS/...` parent folder, same `resolveObsidianVaultPath` helper, same `/api/obsidian/<feature>` route shape. Visual verification requires `npm run dev` on http://localhost:5020/wallet — pending user confirmation. To migrate existing local-only wallets, the next time the dashboard loads with the shared vault enabled it will write through current local state; vault then becomes the source of truth.
- Intended commit message: `Move agent wallets into shared brain`
